name: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb al-Ḍabbī
summary: Basran grammarian of the generation of al-Khalīl, whose circle in the mosque of Basra was a meeting place of scholars, Bedouin and poets; Sībawayh cites him often.
bio: Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb learnt from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and Ibn Abī Isḥāq's circle and taught in Basra for decades; al-Zubaydī places him in the fifth generation with al-Khalīl. His circle drew grammarians, Bedouin who were asked about their speech, and men of letters; Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ heard him, and al-Kitāb cites him some two hundred times, often where he differed from al-Khalīl.

He had his own views on analogy, and the sources give his judgements in disputes: in al-Zubaydī he says that Sībawayh had the truth against al-Aṣmaʿī in a debate he watched, though al-Aṣmaʿī had the readier tongue. He wrote books on the meanings of the Qurʾān and on rare words, which are lost. He died in 182/798, said to be nearly a hundred years old.
